questions.question: Why use RAG instead of simply passing all documents directly into an LLM with a 1M+ token context window?
key_points_to_cover: Inference cost scales with input tokens
Latency increases significantly with very large prompts
'Lost in the Middle' attention degradation phenomenon
Dynamic real-time information retrieval without retraining or repassing entire corpora
Precise source citation and provenance tracking

questions.question: What is Hybrid Search in vector databases, and why does combining dense embeddings with BM25 improve retrieval quality?
key_points_to_cover: Dense vectors capture semantic nuance but fail on exact keyword lookups, rare codes, IDs, and jargon
BM25 is a term-frequency TF-IDF based sparse search that excels at exact lexical matching
Hybrid search merges both score lists using techniques like Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) or convex combination
Prevents false negatives when users search for exact technical terms (e.g. 'CUDA 11.8' vs 'GPU driver')

questions.question: How do you decide on chunk size and chunk overlap when building a RAG ingestion pipeline? What are the trade-offs?
key_points_to_cover: Small chunks: high precision semantic search, but lack global context and sentence boundaries
Large chunks: retain deep contextual meaning, but introduce noise and lower embedding specificity
Overlap (e.g. 10-20%): preserves semantic continuity across chunk boundaries
Semantic chunking / Hierarchical chunking / Parent-Child retrieval as modern mitigations

questions.question: How do you systematically evaluate whether a RAG system is hallucinating or generating accurate answers?
key_points_to_cover: RAG Triad: Context Relevance (retrieval quality), Groundedness / Faithfulness (is output supported by context), Answer Relevance
Evaluation frameworks like Ragas or TruLens using LLM-as-a-Judge
Synthetic test dataset generation from source documents
Golden QA reference datasets with human validation

questions.question: How do you choose between Cosine Similarity, Dot Product, and Euclidean (L2) distance for vector retrieval?
key_points_to_cover: Cosine similarity measures the angle between vectors, normalizing for vector magnitude (ideal for text of varying lengths)
Dot product takes into account both angle and magnitude; identical to cosine similarity when vectors are L2-normalized
Dot product is computationally faster when normalized
Euclidean (L2) measures straight-line geometric distance in space
